entities.summary: Lycosura was a city in the ancient Parrhasia region of south Arcadia said by Pausanias to be the oldest city in the world, although there is no evidence for its existence before the fourth century BCE. Its current significance is chiefly associated with the sanctuary of the goddess Despoina, which contained a colossal sculptural group that Pausanias wrote was made by Damophon of Messene. This group comprises acrolithic-technique statues of Despoina and Demeter seated on a throne, with statues of Artemis and the Titan Anytos standing on either side of them – all in Pentelic marble. Lycosura is a archaeological site from Europe. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Lycosura's sanctuary of Despoina is notable for its well-preserved acrolithic sculptures, which provide valuable insights into ancient Greek art and architecture. The site's historical significance lies in its association with the goddess Despoina and the Damophon sculptural group.
